hazards.evidence: Everyday dishware (stacked plates/bowls, glasses) is kept in an upper glass-front wall cabinet, requiring overhead reaching while using a walker.
Hard kitchen floor in front of the sink/stove is smooth and highly reflective with wet-looking specular patches, indicating a slick surface for a walker.
A freestanding wooden chair sits in the center of the kitchen walkway and the dining set crowds the left side, narrowing/obstructing the walker path between the counter and stove.
The available chair is an armless wooden side chair (no armrests), making sit-to-stand difficult after hip/knee replacement; dining chairs on the left also appear armless.
Room is dim overall (single small pendant, dark foreground/left side) with glare reflected off the glossy floor, reducing visibility of obstacles and floor edges.
A round pet bed and a pet bowl/mat sit on the floor in the kitchen walkway, creating underfoot tripping hazards for someone using a walker.
